==========================================================================
 THE FIVE EXCEPTION CLASSES, EACH WITH ITS OWN k
 (labels are STRUCTURAL since 2026-08-13; the k each one SHOULD measure
  lives in quartus_gate.py's checked `nominal` table, not in a string:
  DEFAULT 1.0 * SAME 2.0 * INTO 1.0 * OUTOF 1.0 * ENABLE 1.0.  A label that
  ASSERTS a k it no longer measures is a flag nobody reads -- which is
  why `CE4` was RENAMED `SAME` at the contract correction.)
==========================================================================

==========================================================================
 THE LADDER BEHIND THE BINDING CONE
==========================================================================

 ⚠ EVERY RUNG IS RESTRICTED TO divclk -> divclk.  Quartus's own Fmax
   Summary note says FMAX is computed ONLY for paths whose source and
   destination are driven by the SAME clock, so a cross-domain path
   (the JTAG hub, the HPS bridge) is not a divclk ceiling and must not
   be quoted as one.  A first run of this script without the filter
   returned the sld_jtag_hub at rung 2; that hit is EXCLUDED here for
   that reason, and this note is why.

--- RUNG 1: not latching in an observation register ---

  k = 1.0000   slack =   -3.573   ->  T_min  34.823 ns  =    28.72 MHz

 Compare against Quartus's OWN Fmax Summary in <rev>.sta.rpt, which is
 the authority.  Its note says it scales the rising and falling edges
 along with FMAX, so it handles the negedge destination itself.
